channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President Visits Modern Pharmaceutical Plant in Tashkent
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the "RomPharm NS" pharmaceutical production facility in Tashkent's Almazar district. The plant aims to supply the domestic market with quality medicines and increase import substitution, with plans to reach an annual capacity of 1 billion tablets and 500 million capsules. The facility, built to EU GMP standards, represents a 45 million euro investment and has created 150 jobs.

item.title: Shanghai Spirit Remains Key for Trust and Cooperation, Says Uzbek Official
item.description: The Shanghai Spirit continues to be vital for strengthening security, economic interaction, and sustainable development amid global changes, according to Ulugbek Shermatov, Chairman of the Legislative Chamber Committee on International Affairs of Uzbekistan. He highlighted the SCO's 25-year evolution into a major international platform and emphasized the role of China in Central Asia's economic resilience through expanding trade ties.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Boost Textile Exports to $4 Billion by 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase its textile exports to $4 billion by the end of 2026, up from $2.6 billion in 2025. A recent dialogue focused on enhancing export potential, removing technical barriers, and implementing international standards for local textile enterprises. Exporters are advised to thoroughly research target market requirements, including certification and product safety regulations, before production.

item.title: Three Arrested After Environmental Inspector Dies in Syrdarya
item.description: Three individuals have been detained on suspicion of causing the death of Mirzo Botirov, a chief specialist with the State Ecological Control Inspectorate. Botirov died during an operation against illegal fishing on September 9, after confronting suspects using electric fishing gear.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Inaugurates Juice Production Subsidiary
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon inaugurated a new juice production subsidiary in the Rasht region during a working visit on September 11. The enterprise aims to develop domestic production, process local raw materials, and increase import-substituting products. It created 17 local jobs and has a production capacity of 1.2 million liters annually.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan aims to resolve textbook deficit by 2030, says publisher
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to fully address its textbook deficit in schools by 2030, according to Tologon Amatov, director of the "Okuu Kitebi" publishing house. The transition to 12-year education necessitates a phased update of the book fund. Millions of textbooks and study materials are being printed, with new domestic textbooks for history and geography under development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prints 20- and 50-som banknotes domestically for first time
item.description: For the first time since independence, Kyrgyzstan has printed 20- and 50-som banknotes domestically, marking a step towards strengthening economic independence. Previously, the national currency was printed abroad for over 30 years. The National Bank did not specify the number of notes printed or when they will enter circulation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Maintain Regulated Fuel Prices Until End of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will keep regulated prices for AI-92 gasoline, diesel, and auto gas until the end of 2026. The Antimonopoly Service has agreements with importers, with the state compensating the difference between import costs and consumer prices. Prices vary by region, with higher rates for remote areas.

item.title: Uzbekistan integrates into the global market through economic reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan has transitioned from a closed, resource-based economy to an open model integrating into the global market. Reforms since 2017, including currency convertibility and tax liberalization, have attracted significant foreign investment into sectors like "green" energy, textiles, and pharmaceuticals. Foreign trade now spans over 160 countries, with key partners including China, Russia, Turkey, and South Korea.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host International Textile Forum 'Tajikistan-2026'
item.description: Dushanbe will host the International Textile Forum 'Tajikistan-2026' on September 23, 2026, organized by the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies. The event aims to discuss industry development, attract foreign investment, share international experience, and showcase the sector's potential, including its use of renewable hydropower and tax incentives.

item.title: Two miners died during tire change operation at a mine in Navoi region
item.description: Two workers died during a tire change operation at a mine in the Navoi region. State supervisory organizations are conducting a special investigation to determine the circumstances and causes of the accident. Further details are available on daryo.uz.

item.title: Uzbekistan expands international cooperation with Sweden and Finland
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Deputy Senate Chairman met with the ambassadors of Sweden and Finland to discuss strengthening bilateral relations, inter-parliamentary cooperation, and trade-economic ties. Key areas for collaboration include education, digital technologies, ecology, water resource management, and think tank exchanges. Regular dialogue between parliamentary groups and cooperation within international organizations were agreed upon.

item.title: Two employees died in an accident during tire fitting at the NKMK "Pistali" mine
item.description: Two employees died in an accident during tire fitting at the "Pistali" mine of the Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Combinat (NKMK). The incident occurred on September 10 around 3:00 PM. Law enforcement agencies and state supervisory organizations are investigating the causes.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Heritage Impact Assessment System for Historical Cities
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to implement a Heritage Impact Assessment (HIA) system to protect its historical cities, including Bukhara, Samarkand, Khiva, Shakhrisabz, and Tashkent. The new system aims to preserve unique historical monuments amidst active construction and infrastructure development. Digital platforms, digital twins, and a cultural heritage situational center are planned.

item.title: Uzbek National Guard Officers to Be Required to Identify Themselves to Citizens
item.description: Amendments to the law "On the National Guard of the Republic of Uzbekistan" were approved, requiring officers to identify themselves when interacting with citizens. This change aims to eliminate legislative duplication and fill practical gaps. The law also refines the guard's duties regarding public order and property protection.

item.title: Russian Interior Ministry reports 40% drop in migrant crime amid increased checks
item.description: Russia's Interior Ministry reports a 40% decrease in crimes committed by migrants. However, the number of checks increased by 155,000, with 43% more individuals screened.

item.title: Russian Interior Ministry reports 40% decrease in crimes by foreign citizens
item.description: Crimes by foreign citizens in Russia decreased by 40% in the first half of 2026, according to the Interior Ministry. This is attributed to expanded powers allowing focus on organized crime and illegal migration.

item.title: Uzbekistan's privatization drive creates new opportunities for private capital
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing measures to reduce state ownership and expand the private sector, including a new privatization phase offering state assets. This initiative, particularly significant for the energy sector, aims to boost efficiency and attract private capital. A presidential decree outlines the sale of stakes in 84 companies, real estate, and land, valued at approximately 100 trillion soums.

item.title: South Korean President invites Central Asian leaders to Seoul for economic summit
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has invited leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan to a summit in Seoul on September 16. The meeting will focus on deepening trade and economic cooperation.

item.title: WHO: 727,000 People Die by Suicide Annually Worldwide
item.description: The World Health Organization reports that approximately 727,000 people die by suicide globally each year. Suicide is the third leading cause of death for individuals aged 15-29. Low- and middle-income countries account for 73% of cases.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Reduce Exceptions for Underage Marriage
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to shorten the list of valid reasons for marriage before the legal age. The government also intends to strengthen accountability for promoting underage marriages. Currently, only two exceptional circumstances allow for such unions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Inaugurates Renovated Manas Ordo Complex in Talas
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov announced that 1.4 billion soms from the state budget were spent on renovating the Manas Ordo national complex in Talas. The renovation aims to create a modern museum combining heritage and technology, including facilities for events and cultural preservation. This initiative is part of Kyrgyzstan's 35th independence anniversary celebrations.

item.title: Eight Injured in Drone Attack on Kyiv, Residential Building Hit
item.description: Russian forces launched a drone attack on Kyiv on September 11, 2026, injuring at least eight people. One drone struck a nine-story residential building in the Dnipro district, causing a fire. Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported fires in the Kyiv region as well, with debris found in multiple areas.

item.title: Financial irregularities totaling 826 million soms found in Balykchy budget
item.description: The Accounts Chamber has identified financial violations amounting to 826.7 million soms in the budget of Balykchy. The city is currently led by Baatyrbek Zhantaev, a relative of presidential affairs administrator Kanybek Tumanbaev.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev holds phone call with Armenian Prime Minister
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev spoke by phone with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on September 11. They discussed developing bilateral relations, particularly in trade, economy, and investment. Both leaders emphasized strengthening regional connectivity through logistics and transport corridors.

item.title: New Tajik Ambassador to Kuwait presents credentials to the Emir
item.description: Khusrav Noziri, the new Ambassador of Tajikistan to Kuwait, presented his credentials to Sheikh Mishal Ahmad Al-Sabah, the Emir of Kuwait, on September 8. The Tajik Embassy in Kuwait announced this development.

item.title: Tajikistan to Host Business Forum 'Tajikistan - Forward' in Dushanbe
item.description: A business forum titled 'Tajikistan - Forward' will be held in Dushanbe on October 14-15, 2026. Organized by the State Committee on Investments, the event aims to foster dialogue, cooperation, and showcase new opportunities in entrepreneurship and investment. It will feature discussions on public-private partnerships, venture capital, and innovation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Armenia to Develop New Industrial Cooperation Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan and Armenia will develop new industrial cooperation projects. Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Nikol Pashinyan discussed trade, investment, and the development of transport and logistics corridors via a phone call. Both nations aim to strengthen economic ties and explore collaborative ventures.

item.title: History of State of Emergency Declarations in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering amendments to constitutional laws on states of emergency. The country has declared states of emergency multiple times since independence, notably in 2010 during political upheaval and ethnic clashes. Military rule has never been declared. The first known emergency was in 1990.

item.title: Bishkek Mayor's Office Responds to Criticism Over Road Quality
item.description: Bishkek's Department of Transport reported defects on approximately 1% of roads built in the last two years, responding to criticism from Vice Speaker Bolot Ibrahimov. The city stated that new roads have a five-year warranty, requiring contractors to fix defects at their own expense. A commission may be formed to inspect road conditions and quality.

item.title: Vietnam's ROX Group Explores Investment Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Vietnam's ROX Group is considering implementing investment projects in Uzbekistan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev discussed cooperation in the energy, geology, finance, and tourism sectors with the company's founder. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Medvedev Calls for Stricter Controls on Migrants in Russia
item.description: Dmitry Medvedev stated that controls on migrants in Russia will be tightened. He emphasized that a migrant's income must be sufficient to support themselves and their family. Those who fail to meet the requirements may have their patents canceled and be forced to leave Russia.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Inaugurates 15 Facilities Remotely
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon remotely commissioned 15 facilities across Rasht, Nurobod, Sangvor, Lakhsh, and Tajikabad districts. He also reviewed a road project. The inaugurated facilities include administrative buildings, educational institutions, a hotel, and infrastructure for national security and food security.

item.title: World Bank outlines financial aid conditions for Tajikistan, proposing up to $1.2 billion
item.description: The World Bank has detailed the conditions for providing financial assistance to Tajikistan. The bank intends to offer funding of up to $1.2 billion to the country. Further details are available.

item.title: Uzbekistan signs law on protecting citizens from noise pollution
item.description: Uzbekistan's president has signed a law protecting citizens from harmful noise. Adopted in October 2025 and approved in June 2026, the law will take effect three months after official publication. It defines permissible noise levels and restricts noisy activities during nighttime and construction.

item.title: Central Asian leaders to meet South Korean president in Seoul next week
item.description: Presidents of Central Asian countries will convene in Seoul next week for the first summit with South Korea. Prior to the summit, President Yoon Suk Yeol will hold separate meetings with the leaders of the five Central Asian nations.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon inaugurates airport, presidential school, and museum in Rasht
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon has commissioned a new airport, a presidential school, and the Nusratullo Maksum Museum in the Rasht district. The inaugurations took place during his working visit to the region. The president also opened other facilities.

item.title: CIS Nations Prepare for Eurasian Antiterror-2026 Exercise
item.description: Experts from Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan participated in a preparatory meeting for the Eurasian Antiterror-2026 exercise. The event, held in Minsk, outlined the exercise's stages, information system usage, and typical scenarios. The full exercise will occur in three phases across six CIS countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Investigates Airline Compensation for Delayed Flights
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee is examining passenger compensation for domestic flights delayed due to airline fault. The committee noted a significant increase in consumer complaints regarding flight delays, lack of timely information, and poor service quality. In some cases, passengers did not receive compensation or alternative solutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Alter Borders of Zarafshon City and Three Districts
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate approved changes to the borders of Zarafshon city in Navoiy region and Jarqo‘rg‘on and Qiziriq districts in Surxondaryo region. Over 2459 hectares will be incorporated into Zarafshon city for industrial and residential development, aiming to boost investment and create jobs.
